problem:
Which of the following elementary row operations transforms the matrix  $C$ into the matrix $D$, where 

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & -1 \\ 7 & 7 & 2 \\ -6 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}-6 & 3 & -3 \\ 7 & 7 & 2 \\ -6 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}]?
$$
worked_solution:
First, notice that the $2$nd and the $3$rd rows are the same in both matrices. The only row that has changed is the $1$st row. 

By considering the given row operations that modify the $1$st row, we notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & -1 \\ 7 & 7 & 2 \\ -6 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=3\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-6 & 3 & -3 \\ 7 & 7 & 2 \\ -6 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =D.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{1}:=3\cdot {R}_{1}.
$$
